I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will follow the cropping pattern that fits my land, water, and labor best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most because it matches the local climate, the local market, and the way I know how to work. I do not have much room to take risks at the start of the season, so I will not spread my land across many crops. I will keep it simple and stable, use improved seed, and manage fertilizer and water carefully so I can protect yield without overspending. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage, apply a moderate base fertilizer with more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at key stages, and spray only when disease or insects are worth controlling. After wheat harvest, I will put the land quickly into summer maize, keep the same field in rotation, use improved seed again, feed it mainly with nitrogen, irrigate a couple of times if rainfall is short, and keep pesticide use limited but timely. This is the plan I would choose because it gives me the most dependable harvest for the year.
